findings.title: enableSqlExpressions reads the feature flag but always returns false
findings.body: The new helper computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false in every branch, so the feature-flag check is dead code and the flag's value is never actually consulted. Since the intent of this PR is to unconditionally disable SQL expressions, this is functionally correct, but the leftover flag evaluation is misleading: a future maintainer may 'fix' the inverted logic (returning `enabled`) and unknowingly re-enable the vulnerable DuckDB code path. The function should simply `return false` (or the call site should hard-code the error) with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264 so the disable cannot be accidentally reverted.

findings.title: User-facing error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is misleading
findings.body: When a user submits a SQL expression, the reader now returns the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented". The feature is in fact implemented but deliberately disabled due to the CVE-2024-9264 RCE/LFI vulnerability; telling users it is 'not implemented' misdirects them (they may enable the sqlExpressions feature flag expecting it to work, or file support tickets). The message should state that SQL expressions are disabled, e.g. "SQL expressions are disabled in this version of Grafana".
